packages.title: 2026 conversion factors activity-input QA
facts: DESNZ 2026 conversion factors calculate GHG emissions from activity data such as fuel volume, purchased electricity kWh or distance travelled.
Activity data are inputs to a calculation rather than parcel-level measured emissions.
The factors are intended for UK activities in 2026.
Users must preserve the activity unit that matches the selected factor.
No parcel value is inferred without verified parcel activity data.

packages.title: 2026 conversion factors Scope 1-2-3 separation QA
facts: The 2026 conversion-factor resource supports Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 reporting separately.
The three scopes describe different emissions-accounting boundaries.
A factor selected for one scope must not be silently relabelled as another scope.
Scope classification is a reporting boundary rather than a cadastral boundary.
No parcel emissions are created from scope labels alone.

packages.title: 2026 conversion factors annual-vintage QA
facts: UK government company-reporting conversion factors are published annually.
The 2026 edition was published on 11 June 2026.
Methodology and major-change documents accompany the annual release.
Year-specific factors should retain their publication vintage for comparable reporting.
A later annual factor must not be retroactively substituted without documenting the change.

packages.title: Activity-based versus spend-based factor QA
facts: DESNZ distinguishes its activity-based conversion factors from Defra spend-based emissions multipliers.
Spend-based methods are primarily intended for expenditure-based supply-chain assessment when detailed activity data are unavailable.
Activity-based and spend-based methods have different inputs and uncertainty structures.
Users should report the method used for emissions accounting.
The two methods are not interchangeable parcel measurements.

packages.title: Conversion factors not statistics themselves QA
facts: DESNZ states the company-reporting conversion factors are not statistics in themselves.
They are a calculation tool used with activity data to estimate emissions.
The resource voluntarily follows the Code of Practice for Statistics to support quality and transparency.
A factor value alone is not an observed emissions total.
No measured parcel emissions are claimed from factor tables.

packages.title: Conversion factors NAEI basis QA
facts: DESNZ states the conversion factors are based primarily on the National Atmospheric Emissions Inventory.
The underlying inventory is updated as new data become available and is subject to quality assurance and review.
Annual methodological improvements can change factor values.
Inventory-derived factors remain model inputs rather than direct site readings.
Methodology provenance is preserved with each QA example.

packages.title: SECR disclosure versus measurement QA
facts: SECR requires in-scope organisations to disclose energy use, GHG emissions and related information in annual reporting.
Corporate disclosure is a reporting process rather than a direct emissions sensor.
Reported figures can be calculated from activity data and government conversion factors.
Company reporting boundaries do not automatically match land-parcel boundaries.
No parcel value is inferred from the existence of a SECR disclosure obligation.

packages.title: ESOS energy audit versus emissions QA
facts: ESOS is an energy-assessment and compliance scheme for qualifying organisations.
An ESOS assessment identifies energy use and energy-saving opportunities.
An audit finding is not the same as a verified GHG inventory total.
Potential energy savings are not automatically realised emissions reductions.
No parcel emissions value is inferred from ESOS qualification or an audit recommendation.

packages.title: UK ETS HSE no allowance-surrender QA
facts: Hospitals and Small Emitters with HSE status do not surrender UK ETS allowances to cover their emissions.
HSE compliance instead uses annual emissions targets.
The HSE opt-out therefore has a different compliance mechanism from full UK ETS participation.
Not surrendering allowances does not mean the installation has zero emissions.
Compliance status is not a parcel emissions value.

packages.title: UK ETS HSE no free-allocation QA
facts: HSE installations are not entitled to UK ETS free allocation.
Free allocation is an allowance-distribution concept rather than measured emissions.
HSE reportable emissions remain subject to monitoring and target compliance.
Allowance entitlement must not be used as a proxy for emissions magnitude.
No parcel allocation is inferred from HSE status.

packages.title: UK ETS HSE annual-target QA
facts: Every scheme year an HSE installation has a target for reportable emissions.
Targets for 2026 to 2030 are based on scheme rules and historical or forecast information where applicable.
A target is a compliance benchmark rather than an observed emissions total.
Reported performance and target values must remain separate.
No parcel measurement is derived from an annual target.

packages.title: UK ETS hospital 85 percent heat criterion QA
facts: An installation can qualify under the hospital route when at least 85% of the heat it produces in a scheme year is used by or supplied to one or more hospitals, subject to other eligibility conditions.
The 85% figure is an eligibility criterion based on heat use.
Heat-use share is not a GHG emissions percentage.
Hospital-service eligibility does not define a cadastral geometry.
No parcel emissions are inferred from the heat criterion.

packages.title: UK ETS small-emitter 25,000 tCO2e threshold QA
facts: For the 2026 to 2030 allocation period, a qualifying small emitter must emit less than 25,000 tonnes CO2e for each scheme year, subject to the full eligibility rules.
The threshold is an eligibility boundary rather than an assigned emissions value.
Being below a threshold does not reveal the installation's exact emissions.
The criterion applies at installation level.
No parcel value is inferred from threshold eligibility.

packages.title: UK ETS small-emitter 35 MW threshold QA
facts: Where applicable, a qualifying small emitter must also have total rated thermal input below 35 MW for the relevant period.
MW is a thermal-input capacity unit rather than a GHG mass unit.
Capacity and emissions must remain separate metrics.
Eligibility requires the full set of scheme conditions, not the MW threshold alone.
No parcel emissions are calculated from thermal capacity.

packages.title: UK ETS ultra-small-emitter 2,500 tCO2e threshold QA
facts: Ultra Small Emitter status is available to qualifying installations emitting less than 2,500 tonnes CO2e under the relevant scheme rules.
The threshold is not the installation's actual emissions value.
USE status concerns a defined installation rather than arbitrary nearby land.
The allocation-period eligibility window and rules must be preserved.
No parcel value is inferred from USE status.

packages.title: UK ETS USE monitoring-threshold QA
facts: Ultra Small Emitters must continue to monitor their emissions.
They must notify the regulator if emissions exceed the agreed threshold.
Monitoring obligations remain even though the installation has USE status.
Threshold exceedance is a compliance event and not itself a parcel measurement.
No unreported emissions value is fabricated.

packages.title: SECR large-business disclosure QA
facts: SECR is a mandatory framework for specified quoted and large unquoted companies and LLPs that meet the applicable criteria.
The framework requires disclosure of energy and carbon information in annual reporting.
Corporate scope is defined by reporting rules rather than property boundaries.
Disclosure requirements do not establish direct measurement at every site.
No parcel emissions value is inferred from company size or reporting status.

packages.title: SECR annual-report filing QA
facts: SECR information is disclosed through annual company reporting filed through the corporate reporting process.
The reporting period must be preserved when comparing organisations or years.
Annual disclosure can combine multiple sites and activities.
An annual company figure must not be assigned to one parcel without verified allocation data.
Reporting frequency is not a measurement frequency.

packages.title: SECR 2026 PIR transparency finding QA
facts: The 2026 SECR post-implementation review reports that the framework contributed to improved transparency and consistency in company energy and carbon reporting.
The review evaluates the reporting regime rather than publishing parcel emissions.
Its evidence includes multiple research methods and administrative information.
A policy-effectiveness finding is not a GHG measurement.
No parcel value is derived from the evaluation conclusion.
